_real_world.variant_scope: FWJ-6C as fitted to the KJ-600 carrier-based AEW&C aircraft (twin-engine installation); same engine family powers the Y-9/KJ-500/KJ-200 land-based transport/AEW aircraft
public_equipment: FWJ-6C (WoJiang-6C) turboprop, 5,100-5,105 shp (~3,805 kW) takeoff power, 6-blade propeller (militaryfactory.com, redstar.gr, army-technology.com)

_provenance.modeling_note: Powerplant for KJ-600 per the task's requirement. This is a turboprop, not a turbofan/turbojet; per the content_schema_spec's Engine module schema there is no dedicated turboprop shaft-power field, so power is entered through the engine.mil_thrust_n/ab_thrust_n keys following the same substitution convention used for the repo's other rotary/propeller-driven engine records (e.g. T700-GE-401C, T56-A-427A). No PRC official disclosure of FWJ-6C output exists; the 5,100-5,105 shp figure is the consistent public figure carried across every Y-9-family aircraft description (Y-9 transport, KJ-500, KJ-200) since the KJ-600 uses the same base engine as this Y-9-derived engine family, per militaryfactory.com's explicit statement that the KJ-600 uses '2 x Zhuzhou WoJiang-6C turboprop engines developing 5,103-5,105 horsepower each.' mil_thrust_n and ab_thrust_n are set equal since a turboprop has no separate afterburning stage; sfc and bypass_ratio have no public figures and are engineering_estimate proxies typical of this turboprop class.

engine.mil_thrust_n.note: 5,103-5,105 shp = ~3,805 kW = 3,805,000 W takeoff power per militaryfactory.com's KJ-600 entry, cross-confirmed by redstar.gr's identical 5,100 shp figure for the same engine on the Y-9/KJ-500/KJ-200 family. Field repurposed to hold power in watts (see modeling_note) rather than a jet-thrust value, following the repo's turboprop engine-record precedent

engine.ab_thrust_n.note: set equal to mil_thrust_n: a turboprop has no distinct afterburning/emergency stage in public sources for this engine, unlike the WZ-10 turboshaft's separately-rated contingency power

engine.sfc_mil.note: engineering_estimate typical of a 5,000+ shp-class modern turboprop; no public FWJ-6C fuel-consumption figure

engine.sfc_ab.note: set equal to sfc_mil, consistent with ab_thrust_n=mil_thrust_n; no distinct afterburning fuel-consumption regime for a turboprop

engine.bypass_ratio.note: 0.0: not applicable to a turboprop engine, matching the repo's convention for propeller-driven engine records
